cards.text: Two angels arrive at Sodom in the evening. Lot, Abraham's nephew, is sitting right in the city gateway (Gen 12:5). When he sees them, he gets up to meet them and bows facedown.

cards.question: Lot invites the two visitors to wash their feet and spend the night at his house. They say yes right away.

cards.text: But Lot insists SO strongly that they follow him home anyway. I know that move, friend. That's me holding out a warm batch to anybody who walks past my oven.

cards.question: Inside, Lot prepares a feast for his two guests. He even bakes ___ bread.

cards.text: Before anyone has gone to bed, there's trouble. All the men of Sodom, young and old, have surrounded Lot's house.

cards.question: The men of Sodom have surrounded Lot's house at night. What do they demand?

answers.text: That Lot send his guests out
That Lot leave the city tonight
That Lot open the city gate

cards.text: They say it plain: “Send them out to us so we can have relations with them!” Lot goes outside to meet them and shuts the door behind him.

cards.question: Outside, Lot calls the men of Sodom his brothers and pleads with them not to do such a wicked thing.

cards.text: Then Lot offers the crowd his two daughters instead. He says his guests have come under the protection of his roof.

cards.question: The crowd tells Lot to get out of the way. What do they say about him?

answers.text: He came as a foreigner and now acts like a judge
He is a spy who came in with the strangers
He owes the whole city a debt he never paid

cards.text: They threaten to treat Lot worse than his guests. Then they press in on him and move in to break down the door.

cards.question: The crowd is pressing in on Lot at his door. What do the two men inside do?

answers.text: Pull Lot inside and shut the door
Step outside to face the crowd
Slip out through the back way

cards.question: Then the two men strike the crowd at the entrance, young and old, with ___.

cards.text: So the men of Sodom wear themselves out trying to find the door. The same door they were just about to break down.
Now the two men ask Lot if he has anyone else in the city who belongs to him, like a son-in-law, sons or daughters. Get them out of here, they say.

cards.question: The two men tell Lot to get his family out of Sodom. Why?

answers.text: They are about to destroy the city
The crowd will be back at dawn
A famine is coming to the plain

cards.text: So Lot goes out to the men pledged to marry his daughters. He tells them, “Get out of this place, for the LORD is about to destroy the city!”

cards.question: Lot warns his future sons-in-law that the LORD is about to destroy Sodom. How do they take it?

answers.text: They run to warn the city
They leave with him that night

cards.text: At daybreak, the angels hurry Lot along. Take your wife and your two daughters, they tell him, or you'll be swept away in the punishment of the city.

cards.question: The angels tell Lot to hurry, and Lot gets moving right away.

cards.text: Lot hesitates. Friend, I've hit snooze on PLENTY of alarms, but never on an ANGEL.

cards.question: The men grab the hands of Lot, his wife and his two daughters and lead them safely out of the city. Why?

answers.text: Because of the LORD's compassion for them
Because Lot paid them for their help
Because Lot's wife begged them to

cards.text: The moment they're out, one of the men gives the order. Run for your lives, flee to the mountains, and don't stop anywhere on the plain.

cards.question: Run to the mountains and don't stop on the plain. What else does the man tell Lot's family NOT to do?

cards.text: But Lot says, “No, my lords, please!” Friend, the man is MID-rescue and he's asking to change the destination.

cards.question: Lot says he can't run to the mountains or the disaster will overtake him. What does he ask for instead?

answers.text: To flee to a small town nearby
To go back for his sons-in-law
To hide out in Abraham's tents

cards.question: The man grants Lot's request and says he will not demolish the town Lot points out.

cards.text: Hurry, the man tells him, because he can't do anything until Lot gets there. By the time the sun has risen over the land, Lot reaches the town, called Zoar.

cards.question: Lot is safe in Zoar. What does the LORD rain down on Sodom and Gomorrah?

cards.text: He destroys those cities and the entire plain, everyone living in the cities and everything that grew on the ground.

cards.question: Remember the order not to look back? Lot's wife looks back. What happens to her?

answers.text: She becomes a pillar of salt
She is swallowed by the earth

cards.text: Early the next morning, Abraham goes back to the place where he had stood before the LORD. That's the spot where he asked the LORD to spare Sodom for the sake of the righteous (Gen 18:23-32).

cards.question: Abraham looks down toward Sodom, Gomorrah and the whole plain. What does he see?

answers.text: Smoke rising like smoke from a furnace
A flood covering the whole plain

cards.question: When God destroyed the cities of the plain, He remembered Abraham and brought Lot out of the catastrophe.
Lot and his two daughters leave Zoar to live in a cave in the mountains. Why does Lot leave Zoar?

answers.text: He is afraid to stay there

cards.text: In that cave, the older daughter says there's no man in the land for them and they need to preserve their father's line. So two nights in a row, the daughters get Lot drunk with wine and sleep with him, and both become pregnant.

cards.question: The older daughter names her son Moab, and the younger names hers Ben-ammi. Which peoples come from these two sons?

cards.text: That's where we'll leave Lot for now, friend. But Abraham's story? Oh, that one's STILL in the oven.

findings.problem: The passage starts in the middle of a thought. 'The two angels' are the visitors who left Abraham in Gen 18, where the LORD said He would go down to see Sodom (Gen 18:20-22). The opening card never says where the two angels came from or why they are going to Sodom.

rule.text: If the passage starts in the middle of a thought, it gives the context.

findings.problem: The joke's core action is Lot refusing to take no for an answer after the guests turn him down. The comparison, Papa Dorin offering a warm batch to passersby, has no refusal to push past, so it isn't the same action. The line also reads like a nice dad being pleasant rather than a real laugh.

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: This card asks the baker to guess what kind of bread Lot bakes. That detail doesn't move the passage forward or help the baker understand it, and it can only be answered by luck.

rule.text: Ask about the moments that move the passage forward and the details the baker needs to understand it.

findings.problem: Gen 19:13 gives the reason for the destruction: the outcry to the LORD against Sodom's people is so great that He has sent them to destroy it. No card in the walkthrough mentions this. It is the key detail explaining why Sodom is destroyed.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: Card 12 already says the LORD destroyed those cities and the entire plain. That rules out the wrong answer 'Both cities still standing,' which leaves only two real choices.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This one story card packs in all of Gen 19:31-36, a narrative stretch and not a long stretch of detail. It covers the older daughter's reasoning, her plan, two nights of getting Lot drunk, both daughters sleeping with him, and both pregnancies. That is far more than two beats. It also leaves out the detail, repeated twice, that Lot was not aware when they lay down or got up (19:33, 35).

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The question names the son Moab, so 'The Moabites and the Ammonites' stands out right away against the other two answers. No reasoning is needed.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: 'That's where we'll leave Lot for now' closely copies the doc's example line ('And that's where we'll leave it for now'). 'For now' also hints that Lot's story continues later in the group, which is a claim about what happens next.

rule.text: It gives nothing away about what happens next. The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This passage has sexual content: the crowd's demand (19:5), Lot offering his daughters (19:8), and the daughters sleeping with their father (19:31-36). The docs say Papa Dorin is always clean and written for adults, but those rules cover his humor. Nothing says how to retell sensitive sexual content in Scripture, or whether to ask choice cards about it. The walkthrough quotes 19:5 directly but folds 19:31-36 into a single story card with no choice cards.
findings.question: How should Prep handle sexual content in a passage? Should it be retold in full and asked about like any other moment, or kept to a short summary story card with no choice cards, and how direct should the wording be?

findings.problem: This card is only the story-isn't-over line and tells no verse, but it cites Genesis 19:38. That verse is already cited by the choice card before it. The docs allow a card that is just this line but don't say what it should cite.
findings.question: What should the 'verses' field be on a final story card that only carries the story-isn't-over line: the passage's last verse, null, or something else?
